spec.name: url-shortener-short
spec.title: URL shortener
spec.requirement:
# URL shortener

- Create a short link for a long http(s) URL; return the short code and short URL.
- Redirect a short link to its original URL; unknown codes return 404.
- Optional custom alias (3-32 letters, digits, `_` or `-`); a taken alias returns 409.
- Show a link's click count.
- Reject invalid URLs with 422.
- Tech stack: Java with Spring Boot (Maven), JUnit for tests.
- Provide documented commands to run the service and its tests.

stage_guidance.guidance: Pin down ambiguities: allowed URL schemes (http/https only), max URL length, alias case sensitivity, whether alias may collide with reserved paths, whether a redirect counts as a click, redirect status (302 vs 301), and 422 vs 400 for malformed JSON.

Keep it minimal: in-memory ConcurrentHashMap store with atomic putIfAbsent for alias uniqueness and AtomicLong click counter; state the persistence ceiling explicitly. Document exact run and test commands (mvn spring-boot:run, mvn test). Use Java and Spring Boot versions that are available locally.

Validate URLs with java.net.URI (scheme http/https, host present) and alias with regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$. Map errors: invalid URL/alias 422, taken alias 409, unknown code 404. Generated codes must not collide with existing codes or aliases. Include MockMvc tests for each requirement bullet and a concurrency check on alias creation.
Run mvn test from a clean state; confirm Maven and a JDK are present and report clearly if the toolchain is missing.
Check open redirect and scheme abuse (javascript:, data:, file:), unbounded URL length, alias path-reserved collisions, and unbounded memory growth.
README must contain verified run and test commands and the API with example requests and status codes.

risks_to_watch: Maven or JDK may be missing or mismatched with the Spring Boot version, blocking build and test evidence.
Weak URL validation allowing non-http(s) schemes or malformed hosts.
Race condition on alias creation or click counting giving wrong 409 or counts.
Random code generation colliding with custom aliases.
In-memory storage loses data on restart and grows unbounded; must be documented as a known limitation.
Status code mapping drift (422 vs 400 from Spring default validation handling).

data.summary: New project: Spring Boot (Maven) URL shortener with create, redirect, custom alias, click count and validation, tested with JUnit and documented run/test commands.
data.problem: Build a new Java Spring Boot (Maven) service that creates short codes for http(s) URLs, redirects them, supports unique custom aliases, tracks click counts and rejects invalid input, with JUnit tests and documented run/test commands.

statements.text: Creating a short link for a long http(s) URL returns the short code and the short URL.
Requesting a short link redirects to its original URL.
Requesting an unknown short code returns 404.
A caller may supply an optional custom alias of 3-32 characters (letters, digits, '_' or '-') which is used as the short code.
Creating a link with an alias that is already taken returns 409.
A link's click count can be retrieved.
Invalid URLs (and invalid aliases) are rejected with 422.
The service is implemented in Java with Spring Boot, built with Maven, and tested with JUnit.
Documented commands are provided to run the service and to run its tests.

ambiguities.question: Which schemes are valid, is there a maximum URL length, and must a host be present?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Only http and https with a non-empty host are valid; maximum length 2048 characters; anything else returns 422.

ambiguities.question: Are aliases case sensitive, and may an alias collide with reserved paths (e.g. 'api', 'links')?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Aliases are case sensitive; aliases equal to reserved route names are rejected with 422; generated codes are 7 alphanumeric characters and never collide with existing codes.

ambiguities.question: Does every successful redirect count as one click, and is reading the click count itself a click?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Each successful redirect increments the count by one; unknown codes and stats reads do not; the count is returned by a stats endpoint (GET /api/links/{code}).

ambiguities.question: Which redirect status should be used, 301 (cacheable) or 302?
ambiguities.default_assumption: 302 Found with a Location header, so browsers do not cache it and clicks keep being counted.

ambiguities.question: Should malformed JSON or a missing url field return 422 or 400?
ambiguities.default_assumption: Missing or invalid field values return 422; unparseable JSON bodies return 400.

requirements.summary: New project: Spring Boot (Maven) URL shortener with create, redirect, custom alias, click count and validation, tested with JUnit and documented run/test commands.

data.summary: New project: in-memory Spring Boot URL shortener. Main risks are abuse of redirects (unsafe schemes, open redirect, SSRF-style targets), alias/code collisions and click-counter races under concurrency, unbounded in-memory growth, and data loss on restart. There is no existing project, so regression and schema migration risk is limited to future changes; the in-memory store has no migration but a later switch to a database would need one.

risks.title: Unsafe URL schemes or hosts accepted (javascript:, data:, file:, missing host, userinfo tricks)
risks.mitigation: Parse with java.net.URI, allow only http/https (case-insensitive), require non-empty host, cap length at 2048, reject control characters/whitespace and userinfo; return 422. Validate at the create endpoint only, never trust stored values on redirect.
risks.validation: Parameterized JUnit test posting javascript:alert(1), data:text/html,x, file:///etc/passwd, ftp://x, http://, 'http://a b', HTTP://ok.com (accepted), a 2049-char URL and a null/blank url; assert 422 for each invalid case and 201 for valid ones.

risks.title: Open redirect and phishing abuse: service redirects to arbitrary attacker URLs
risks.mitigation: Accept as inherent to a public shortener but document it; use 302 with only the stored Location header, strip CR/LF from the Location value (reject at validation), add X-Content-Type-Options and Referrer-Policy headers, and note rate limiting/blocklist as follow-up before public exposure.
risks.validation: Test that redirect response has status 302, a single Location header equal to the stored URL, and that URLs containing %0d%0a or raw CR/LF are rejected at create time with 422 (no header injection). Security review checklist item in the security stage.

risks.title: Custom alias collision race: two concurrent creates of the same alias both succeed
risks.mitigation: Use ConcurrentHashMap.putIfAbsent (or computeIfAbsent) as the single atomic check-and-insert; map a failed insert to 409. Do not use containsKey followed by put.
risks.validation: JUnit concurrency test: N=50 threads (CountDownLatch start) create the same alias; assert exactly one 201 and N-1 409, and the stored URL belongs to the winner.

risks.title: Generated code collides with an existing code or custom alias, overwriting a link
risks.mitigation: Generate 7-char codes with SecureRandom over [A-Za-z0-9] and insert via putIfAbsent in a bounded retry loop (e.g. 10 attempts, then 500/503); generated and custom codes share one keyspace and one atomic insert.
risks.validation: Unit test with an injected code generator that returns a duplicate first then a unique value: assert the existing link is untouched and the new link gets the second code; test that exhausted retries return an error without overwriting.

risks.title: Click counter lost updates under concurrent redirects
risks.mitigation: Store clicks as AtomicLong (or LongAdder) in the link record and increment only on successful redirect lookup; never read-modify-write on a plain long.
risks.validation: JUnit test: 100 threads x 10 redirects to one code, then GET /api/links/{code} returns exactly 1000; also assert unknown code redirects (404) and stats reads do not change the count.

risks.title: Alias collides with reserved routes or is case/format ambiguous, shadowing API endpoints
risks.mitigation: Enforce regex ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$ using full match (not find), treat aliases as case sensitive, and reject reserved names (api, links, actuator, error, h2-console) with 422. Keep API under /api so a root-level {code} route cannot clash.
risks.validation: Parameterized test: aliases 'ab', 33 chars, 'a b', 'a/b', 'a.b', unicode, trailing newline 'abc\n' and 'api' return 422; 'abc', 'A_b-9', 32 chars return 201; 'Abc' and 'abc' coexist as distinct links.

risks.title: Unbounded in-memory growth enables memory exhaustion (DoS)
risks.mitigation: Cap URL length at 2048 and request body size (server.tomcat.max-http-form-post-size / spring.codec max in-memory), and document the limit; add a max link count or rate limiting as a follow-up before public exposure.
risks.validation: Test that an oversized body (e.g. 1 MB) is rejected with 4xx and never stored; review confirms no unbounded collections besides the link map, which is documented as a known ceiling.

risks.title: Data loss on restart: all links and click counts are in memory
risks.mitigation: State clearly in README that storage is in-memory and ephemeral; hide storage behind one small store class so a database can replace it later. No schema or migration exists in this new project; a future persistence change must add a migration plan.
risks.validation: README review confirms the ephemeral-storage warning; a test of the store class through its public methods only, so a later persistent implementation can reuse it.

risks.title: Wrong status codes and error mapping (400 vs 422, 404 vs 405, 409) break the contract
risks.mitigation: Add a @RestControllerAdvice mapping MethodArgumentNotValidException and custom validation errors to 422, HttpMessageNotReadableException to 400, unknown code to 404, taken alias to 409; return a JSON error body without stack traces or internal details.
risks.validation: MockMvc tests for: missing url field (422), malformed JSON (400), unknown code on redirect and on stats (404), duplicate alias (409); assert the body has no exception class names or stack traces.

risks.title: Redirect cached by browsers (301) causes undercounted clicks
risks.mitigation: Use 302 Found and set Cache-Control: no-store on redirect responses.
risks.validation: MockMvc test asserts redirect status is 302, Location equals the original URL, and the Cache-Control header is present.

risks.title: Short URL built from the Host header allows host-header poisoning in returned shortUrl
risks.mitigation: Build shortUrl from a configured base-url property (default http://localhost:8080) rather than the incoming Host/X-Forwarded-Host header.
risks.validation: MockMvc test sends a create request with a spoofed Host: evil.example header and asserts the returned shortUrl starts with the configured base URL.

risks.title: Unverified agent-written code: hallucinated APIs, wrong dependency versions, tests that pass vacuously, undocumented commands that do not work
risks.mitigation: Pin the Spring Boot parent version in pom.xml, use only spring-boot-starter-web, -validation and -test, run the build in a clean checkout, and have the release stage execute the exact documented commands rather than assume them. Review tests for real assertions on every statement S1-S7.
risks.validation: From a clean clone run the README commands verbatim (mvn test and mvn spring-boot:run plus curl smoke for create/redirect/stats); require BUILD SUCCESS and a traceability check that each of S1-S7 has at least one asserting test; mutation spot check by breaking the 409 and 404 branches and confirming tests fail.

risks.title: Dependency and supply-chain exposure from Maven dependencies
risks.mitigation: Keep the dependency set minimal, rely on the Spring Boot BOM for managed versions, avoid extra libraries for URL validation, and note an OWASP dependency-check or Dependabot step for later.
risks.validation: Review the pom.xml dependency list (only starters web, validation, test) and run mvn dependency:tree to confirm no unexpected artifacts.

risks.title: Privacy: stored long URLs may contain tokens or personal data and are logged
risks.mitigation: Do not log full target URLs or request bodies at INFO level; no client IP or user data is stored; document that URLs are stored in plain text and exposed through the stats endpoint to anyone knowing the code.
risks.validation: Run a create and redirect with a URL containing a fake token, grep the application log output and assert the token does not appear; README review confirms the note.

adr.decision: In-memory ConcurrentHashMap store behind one LinkStore class; no database.
adr.rationale: Minimal for the requirement and orchestrator guidance. putIfAbsent gives atomic uniqueness for both aliases and generated codes. Persistence ceiling: all links and clicks are lost on restart and memory is unbounded; a database implementation can replace LinkStore later with its own migration plan.

adr.decision: Redirect with 302 Found and Cache-Control: no-store; redirect route is root-level GET /{code}, API under /api.
adr.rationale: Human decision A4. 302 plus no-store keeps clicks counted. Separate /api prefix plus reserved-name rejection means a code can never shadow an API route.

adr.decision: Clicks are AtomicLong in the Link record, incremented only on successful redirect lookup.
adr.rationale: Avoids lost updates under concurrent redirects without locks; stats reads never count.

adr.decision: Hand-written URL validation with java.net.URI in LinkService; Bean Validation only for presence/shape of fields, mapped to 422.
adr.rationale: No extra libraries; scheme/host/length/control-char rules from clarify A1 are not expressible with @URL alone. Single validation point at create; redirect trusts only stored validated values.

adr.decision: Pin Spring Boot parent 3.5.6 and java.version 17.
adr.rationale: 3.5.6 is available in the local Maven cache (offline reproducible); JDK 25 is installed locally and compiles release 17 bytecode.

assumptions: Maven (mvn) and JDK are on PATH, and Boot 3.5.6 artifacts are in ~/.m2 or Maven Central is reachable during setup.
Service listens on default port 8080 and sits behind no proxy; app.base-url is set per deployment.
Exhausted code-generation retries return 503 (practically unreachable with 62^7 keyspace).
The service is not exposed publicly as-is; rate limiting and blocklists are follow-up before public exposure.
tradeoffs: In-memory store: simplest and race-free via ConcurrentHashMap, but not durable and not shared across instances.
Hand-rolled validation over a validation library: fewer dependencies, slightly more code to test.
302 over 301: every click hits the service (accurate counts) at the cost of no browser/CDN caching.
Root-level /{code} gives short URLs, requiring reserved-name rejection for aliases.
limitations: All links and click counts are lost on restart (ephemeral, documented in README).
No cap on number of links and no rate limiting: memory exhaustion/abuse possible if exposed publicly.
Open redirect / phishing abuse is inherent to a public shortener; only scheme/host validation is done, no SSRF target or blocklist filtering of private hosts.
Stored URLs are plain text and readable by anyone who knows the code via the stats endpoint.
Single instance only; no authentication, no link deletion or expiry.

If persistence is added later, that release must carry its own forward/backward migration plan.

findings.detail: The links ConcurrentHashMap has no maximum size, TTL or eviction, and POST /api/links has no authentication or rate limiting. Any client can create links in a loop (each up to 2048 chars of URL plus a 32-char alias) until the heap is exhausted, which is a denial of service. Add a configurable max link count (reject with 503/429 when full) and per-client rate limiting before any public exposure. Risk R7 asked for this as a follow-up, so no code mitigation exists yet.

The body limit only checks the declared Content-Length. A request with Transfer-Encoding: chunked reports -1, passes the check and is fully buffered by Jackson in @RequestBody, so the 8192-byte limit (app.max-body-bytes) is not enforced. The class comment acknowledges this. Wrap the request in a size-counting stream, or set server.tomcat.max-swallow-size and a bounded-body mechanism, so oversized chunked bodies are rejected. This weakens the R7 mitigation.
